identity.title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNA delivery enables protein expression in chicken testes.

content.abstract: RNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are emerging tools for poultry vaccination, but methods for local protein expression in reproductive tissues remain underdeveloped. Here, we established RNA delivery to chicken testes using LNPs formulated with the ionizable lipid DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3) and multifocal intratesticular injection through an intercostal surgical approach. Bilateral injections were completed in all six chickens in a surgical-feasibility cohort, with postoperative recovery during the 7-day observation period. At an equal RNA mass dose of 80 microg per testis, conventional messenger RNA (mRNA) encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP) produced detectable reporter signals at days 1, 3, and 7, with the highest measured signal at day 3. An eGFP self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) construct showed delayed detectable expression at days 3 and 7. Delivery of mRNAs encoding CRISPR-associated protein 9 (Cas9) and the epitope-tagged recombination-related proteins DNA meiotic recombinase 1 (DMC1) and RAD51 recombinase (RAD51) also produced detectable proteins in testicular tissue. Following local delivery, testicular architecture was preserved, with minimal apoptosis and only a modest inflammatory response. These findings establish the feasibility of local RNA-LNP delivery for short-term protein production in chicken testes, providing a platform for future studies of male reproduction and genome editing.
